newsitem.title: USA: Hughes open to various capital structures.
newsitem.headline: Hughes open to various capital structures.

text.p: Hughes Electronics Corp chief executive officer C. Michael Armstrong said he would consider a variety of alternative capital structures in the wake of his company's acquisition of a 71 percent stake in PanAmSat Corp.

In particular, Armstrong left open the possibility of a spin-off of Hughes's businesses from parent General Motors Corp. He was responding to a reporter's question at a press conference held in New York on Friday afternoon following the announcement of the $3 billion PanAmSat deal.
"Whatever capital structure we need in order to be competitive we will so implement," Armstrong said, when asked about a possible Hughes spinoff from its parent.

He noted that Hughes has a diversified portfolio of direct and indirect satellite investments, including a 60 percent stake in a Latin American direct broadcast to home satellite consortium, a 27 percent stake in American Mobile Satellite Corp as well as the backing of AT&T Corp, which holds a 2.5 percent interest in Hughes DirectTV.
"I think you see a company that has flexibility in its capital structure," he said.
Armstrong said the PanAmSat deal would be "accretive to earnings from the outset."

Although telecommunications services now account for less than five percent of Hughes Electronics revenues, Armstrong said its satellite properties represent the fastest growing percentage of its business.
The vast bulk of Hughes revenues and profits continued to come from its defense electronics and auto parts businesses.
Armstrong said a primary attraction of PanAmSat was its better than 70 percent operating profit margins.
"I wish I had the opportunity every week to consider acquisitions in a market that is exploding" as fast as PamAmSat, he said.
Armstrong said telecommunications services would be Hughes' primary source of growth for the future.
"If you ask me five years from now, it's going to be a big part of our company," he said referring to the company's communications services business.
The Hughes executive said the PamAmSat deal will allow broadcasters to have one-stop shopping for global communications services.
